Subject: Initial: international transfer controls (SCCs / UK addendum / TIA)

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal team is reviewing the DPA and needs to confirm the following before we can move to signature:

1) Do you have an updated list of subprocessors with geolocation (EU/US/APAC) and last-processed date?
2) Can you confirm whether Redwood will execute the EU SCCs + UK Addendum (IDTA) as a single instrument, or if you require separate signature flows?
3) Globex must complete a Transfer Impact Assessment (TIA) for some EU -> US paths; we need any documentation you have showing technical and organizational measures (encryption in transit/rest, key management, data residency controls, access controls, logging/audit).

Attached is a short questionnaire from our privacy team for your ops/legal to fill (TIA questionnaire). Also: timeline is tight — we are targeting contract execution by 2026-07-30. Can you confirm feasibility and point people we should coordinate with?

Thanks,
Emma Clarke
Senior Counsel, Globex Financial

Emma —

Appreciate the clear list. Short answers up-front:
- We can provide an up-to-date subprocessors CSV with regions and last-processed timestamps (attaching v3).
- Redwood is prepared to execute the EU SCCs with the standard UK IDTA addendum; we can offer a combined signature flow (single envelope + UK addendum included) or separate instruments if your procurement prefers. Either is fine; we default to combined to minimize paperwork.
- I’m attaching a high-level TIA evidence packet and our security controls summary. Rishi (legal) and Monica (CS / onboarding) are copied and will follow up on details and specific questionnaire answers.

We can realistically aim for execution by 2026-07-30 provided we close a small set of open points below — will schedule a short call if helpful.

Action items
- Rishi: confirm any redlines to the UK addendum and DPA.
- Monica: prepare onboarding timeline + data residency options for Globex test/staging.
- Aisha: confirm commercial timeline and whether credits/conditional provisions are needed for procurement.

Subject: Re: Data transfer controls — proposed UK IDTA adjustments and subprocessor question

Emma / team,

Thanks — I reviewed the questionnaire and have a couple of legal/operational clarifications:

1) Subprocessors: our CSV identifies current subprocessors and whether they perform storage, inference, or logging. We regularly update the list; we propose a 30-day notice period for subprocessor additions in the DPA (we can support emergency short-notice exceptions).

2) UK Addendum: I have a tracked-change draft attached that is compatible with executing the EU SCCs and the UK IDTA as a single execution flow. There are two points Globex may want to consider:
   - Clause 6.2 (restricted international routing): we propose a technical-caveat clause to allow short-term cross-border cache replication for performance (documented and auditable).
   - Clause 9 (audit rights): we include audit evidence via our SOC 2 report and access to specific logs; full on-site audits are limited to high-risk cases — we can negotiate remote evidence exchange.

3) TIA evidence: our security packet includes TLS enforcement, FIPS CSP for keys, separation of duties, and KV cache control notes. For EU->US transfers specifically, we provide encryption-at-rest with keys managed in our KMS (customer-managed KMS option available for dedicated/private deployments).

Please review the attached redline and the subprocessors CSV. If Globex wants any additional contractual guarantees for particular subprocessors (e.g., data residency clauses), flag them and we’ll route to engineering for feasibility.

I can jump on a 30-min call this afternoon if that helps.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Thanks Rishi — useful detail. A few follow-ups from the Globex privacy review: 

- The 30-day notice for subprocessors is acceptable, but we request a right to review new EU-affecting subprocessors before they go live for at least high-risk categories (storage and logging).
- On Clause 6.2: we need the replication/edge-caching carveout to be explicit that it won’t be used for US-hosted fallback unless documented and authorized.
- Audit evidence: please provide the most recent SOC 2 Type II summary and a sample audit log export format (for our security team's review).

We have redlines in your draft; I’ll send a marked-up version (DocuSign-ready) by EOD and propose a 30-min sync tomorrow at 10:00am BST if that works for Redwood.

Emma
Senior Counsel, Globex Financial

Emma / Globex team —

Thanks — good clarity. Quick confirmation and plan from Redwood:

1) Subprocessors: we will provide a 2-column change log for any additions impacting EU data and flag high-risk categories. We accept the review right for high-risk EU-affecting subprocessors with a 10-business-day review window; if no objection is raised, Redwood may proceed.

2) Clause 6.2 carveout: we will update the draft to explicitly require documented authorization and a fallback checklist before any US-hosted fallback is used.

3) Evidence pack: Monica will share SOC 2 Type II summary and a sanitized sample log export. Rishi will prepare the final UK addendum redline addressing your audit and caching points.

4) Call: tomorrow 10:00am BST works — Aisha will confirm and send a calendar invite (she's arranging procurement details).

Action items (owners):
- Monica: upload SOC2 summary + sample logs to Drive link and share with Emma (by 2026-07-22 09:00 BST).
- Rishi: finalize UK addendum redline and mark clauses for remote audit evidence (by EOD 2026-07-21).
- Aisha: calendar invite + procurement checklist, confirm signature flow preference (single combined envelope) (by 2026-07-21 18:00 BST).

We’re aligned to the 2026-07-30 target; thanks all.
